title: The Roman practice: relics, images, feasts, sodalities, and vows
source_text: VII. Itaque per totam Ecclesiam Romanam usitatum esse Sanctos in aedibus illis dicatis, & de illorum nomine nuncupatis, variis ritibus colere, coram eorum reliquiis, statuis, & imaginibus corpus inclinando & genua flectendo, cereos accendendo, & adolendo thura, ac donaria omnis generis illis offerendo. Quibus addunt dies festos qui sunt peculiariter Sanctorum cultui dicati; & sodalitia quoque de Sanctorum nomine vocata, & in eorum honorem singulariter instituta: atque etiam frequentia vota, quae Sanctis religiose nuncupant & exsolvunt.
pass_a_gloss: And so throughout the Roman Church it is usual to cultivate the Saints with various rites in those dedicated buildings named after them, bowing the body and bending the knees before their relics, statues, and images, lighting candles, burning incense, and offering them gifts of every kind. To these they add feast days peculiarly dedicated to the cult of the Saints, and also sodalities called by the Saints' names and singularly instituted in their honor, and likewise frequent vows which they religiously make to the Saints and pay.
pass_b_english: Across the Roman Church, Saints are honored in churches named for them.
The rites include bows and kneeling before relics, statues, and images, with candles, incense, and offerings.
Feast days, named confraternities, and vows made and paid to the Saints belong to the same practice.

choices.why: Named confraternities are part of the public cult, not private devotion only.
